hints: Express the height of $A$ above the ground at time $t$: $h_A = 20t - 5t^2$.
Express the height of $B$ at time $t$ (which moves for duration $t - 1$): $h_B = 40 - 5(t - 1)^2$.
Equate $h_A = h_B$ to find the collision time $t$.
Substitute $t$ back into $h_A$ to determine the collision height.
walkthrough:
Write the vertical height of particle $A$ above the ground at time $t\text{ s}$:
$$h_A = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 20t - 5t^2$$

Write the vertical height of particle $B$ above the ground, which is dropped from rest at height $40\text{ m}$ at time $t = 1\text{ s}$:
$$h_B = 40 - \frac{1}{2}g(t - 1)^2 = 40 - 5(t - 1)^2$$

Set $h_A = h_B$ to find the time of collision:
$$20t - 5t^2 = 40 - 5\left(t^2 - 2t + 1\right)$$
$$20t - 5t^2 = 40 - 5t^2 + 10t - 5$$
$$20t = 35 + 10t \implies 10t = 35 \implies t = 3.5\text{ s}$$

Calculate the collision height using the position of $A$:
$$h = 20(3.5) - 5(3.5^2) = 70 - 5(12.25) = 70 - 61.25 = 8.75\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Model the position of particle $A$ launched from the ground ($h = 0$) at $t = 0$ with $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
Taking upwards as positive with $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$h_A(t) = 20t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 20t - 5t^2$$

Model the position of particle $B$ released from rest at $h = 40\text{ m}$ at $t = 1\text{ s}$:
Since $B$ begins moving $1\text{ s}$ later, its flight time is $t - 1$ for $t \ge 1$:
$$h_B(t) = 40 - \frac{1}{2}(10)(t - 1)^2 = 40 - 5(t - 1)^2$$

Equate the two positions to find the collision time:
$$20t - 5t^2 = 40 - 5(t - 1)^2$$
Expand the right-hand side:
$$(t - 1)^2 = t^2 - 2t + 1$$
$$40 - 5(t^2 - 2t + 1) = 40 - 5t^2 + 10t - 5 = 35 - 5t^2 + 10t$$
Equate:
$$20t - 5t^2 = 35 - 5t^2 + 10t$$
Add $5t^2$ to both sides and subtract $10t$:
$$10t = 35 \implies t = \frac{35}{10} = 3.5\text{ s}$$

Calculate the collision height above the ground:
$$h = 20(3.5) - 5(3.5)^2 = 70 - 5 \times 12.25 = 70 - 61.25 = 8.75\text{ m}$$

hints: Calculate the velocity of $A$ at $t = 3.5\text{ s}$ using $v_A = u - gt$.
Calculate the velocity of $B$ after falling for $2.5\text{ s}$ using $v_B = -g(t - 1)$.
Take the absolute values to find the speeds of each particle and subtract them.
walkthrough:
Calculate the velocity of particle $A$ at $t = 3.5\text{ s}$ (taking upwards as positive):
$$v_A = u - gt = 20 - 10(3.5) = 20 - 35 = -15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus, the speed of $A$ is $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Calculate the velocity of particle $B$ at $t = 3.5\text{ s}$, which has been falling from rest for $t - 1 = 2.5\text{ s}$:
$$v_B = 0 - g(t - 1) = -10(2.5) = -25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus, the speed of $B$ is $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Find the difference in speeds between the two particles:
$$\text{Difference in speeds} = |v_B| - |v_A| = 25 - 15 = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the kinematic velocity equation under gravity:
$$v = u + at$$
For particle $A$ ($u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $t = 3.5\text{ s}$):
$$v_A = 20 - 10 \times 3.5 = 20 - 35 = -15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The negative sign indicates it is descending. Its speed is:
$$\text{Speed}_A = |v_A| = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

For particle $B$ dropped from rest ($u = 0$, $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, time elapsed $\Delta t = 3.5 - 1 = 2.5\text{ s}$):
$$v_B = 0 - 10 \times 2.5 = -25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Its speed is:
$$\text{Speed}_B = |v_B| = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the difference in their speeds:
$$\text{Difference} = 25 - 15 = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
